summary: Added docs/structure.md as a short repository navigation guide covering top-level layout, data paths, utilities, Docker stack, web demo, and where to find key components.

summary: Planning Agent (2/7): Added utils/planner/discovery.py — a per-request content-probe liveness layer (connect + non-trivial node count + expected-label check, not a bare socket open), each probe bounded by its own short timeout in a daemon thread, with a short-TTL re-probe cache. Reuses the graph_loader Neo4j/Gremlin stores. 9 unit tests plus a verified live read of the running Docker stack (CAPEC live with 4888 nodes in Gremlin; Neo4j correctly marked down on auth failure).
why: Gives the planner a ground-truth view of which graphs are actually loaded right now so it routes only to live sources and marks parts needing a down source unsupported.

summary: Planning Agent (3/7): Added utils/planner/schema.py (machine-readable Plan: sub-questions with required per-sub-question Limits, declared joins, explicit unsupported parts, rationale/assumptions, partial flag, JSON round-trip) and utils/planner/gate.py — a fully deterministic self-evaluation gate validating that every named source is live, every entity exists in that source's card, declared join keys are real and canonical, per-sub-question limits are present and within card bounds, and the plan is non-degenerate. 17 unit tests.
why: This is the planner's core safety mechanism: the LLM drafts and deterministic code grades, so unroutable plans are rejected with specific reasons before they ship.

summary: Planning Agent (4/7): Added the PlanDrafter protocol with a card-grounded DeterministicDrafter (keyword routing over labels/relationships/glosses that builds gate-valid plans by construction, marks down/unsupported parts, records rationale+assumptions) and a configurable OpenAICompatibleDrafter posting to a local /v1/chat/completions endpoint (default localhost:9090 / default-model) with robust JSON extraction and DrafterUnavailable fallback. A HybridDrafter falls back to deterministic when the LLM is unreachable. 29 unit tests incl. a guarded live test; verified the real model emits a gate-valid partial plan against the live CAPEC-up/ATT&CK-down environment.
why: Provides the probabilistic drafting seam behind a protocol so the LLM drafts and deterministic code grades, with an always-available deterministic fallback for testing and offline use.

summary: Planning Agent (5/7): Added utils/planner/agent.py — the bounded self-evaluating ReAct loop (PlanningAgent.plan): re-probe live sources, draft, deterministically gate, feed specific rejection reasons back into the next draft, cap at max_iterations, and on exhaustion degrade to an honest partial plan (keep gate-valid parts via gate.valid_subset, surface the rest as unsupported, never loop forever or fabricate, never emit a degenerate plan as success). Recorded a per-iteration trace, refined the deterministic drafter's gloss matching to curb over-decomposition, and exported PlanningAgent. 7 loop tests; verified end-to-end against the live env with both deterministic and LLM drafters.
why: Ties discovery, drafting, and the gate into one terminating entry point that always emits a routable or honestly-partial plan with an inspectable trace.

summary: Planning Agent (6/7): Added utils/planner/evaluation/ — a plan-level scorer (source-selection precision/recall, unnecessary-source-call count, expected-entity recall, schema adherence via the gate, and honesty/partial correctness, decoupled from downstream answer success), a 7-case expected-plan corpus with dev and holdout splits including out-of-scope and source-down cases, a run_corpus runner, and a run_eval CLI. Added stub_live_view for deterministic scoring. 9 tests; deterministic agent passes the corpus 7/7 (schema/source-recall/honesty all 1.0).
why: Scores the planner on its plan output against fixed reference plans so a good plan is never blamed for a downstream failure, with a frozen holdout split guarding against overfitting.

summary: Planning Agent (7/7): Wired the --plan/--plan-llm CLI (utils/planner/cli.py + main.py) to probe the live graphs and emit the routing plan as JSON; added docs/planner_agent.md (contract, discovery, gate, drafters, plan schema, config), and updated README, docs/structure.md, and docs/goals.md to mark the Wk 6-7 planning agent complete and document utils/planner. Verified --plan end-to-end against the live stack (CAPEC live, ATT&CK down -> partial plan) with both deterministic and LLM drafters. 3 CLI tests; full planner suite (88) green.
why: Makes the planning agent runnable from the CLI over the live graphs and documents its contract, completing the planning-agent deliverable.

summary: Added notebooks/planner_playground.ipynb — an interactive notebook to drive the planning agent: probe live graphs, inspect source cards and the canonical join key, plan questions with a plan_question() helper (deterministic and local-LLM drafters), run a batch incl. out-of-scope/partial cases, dump the full machine-readable plan, and score the expected-plan corpus. Robust repo-root path setup so imports work from notebooks/. Executed end-to-end headlessly against the live stack (exit 0).

summary: Planning Agent fix: the deterministic drafter now requires at least one identifier (node-label/relationship-name) match to select a source; a lone gloss/description match no longer pulls a whole source in or fabricates a spurious cross-source join. _match_card returns id_hits/gloss_hits separately and selection gates on id_hits>0. Fixes over-selection where e.g. 'which groups use which techniques' routed to both ATT&CK and CAPEC. Added a regression test; full planner suite (89) and eval corpus (7/7, 0 unnecessary calls) green.
why: The keyword fallback over-selected sources on weak description-level matches, producing confusing cross-source plans for single-source questions.

summary: Added --yolo-all single-command pipeline flag. Running uv run main.py --yolo-all now orchestrates the full stack in one invocation: download datasets, build canonical artifacts, check credentials (non-interactive), start Docker, load ATT\u0026CK into Neo4j and CAPEC into Gremlin, then verify both graphs. Each step prints a live status line; a Unicode box-drawing summary table is printed at the end. Already-done steps are skipped automatically.
why: The user had to run six or more separate commands to go from a fresh checkout to a running stack. A single entry-point reduces friction and makes onboarding trivial.

summary: Error-Handling (0/4): Authored docs/plans/error-handling-recovery-plan.md, a 4-step plan to make the --yolo-all pipeline self-heal. Root cause of 'relationship type not in schema': the builder writes canonical artifacts into an un-cleaned existing directory and _step_build skips rebuilding when a stale manifest is present, so on-disk artifacts can disagree with the freshly written allowlist schema.
why: Plan the requested recovery policy (back up + rebuild on existing-artifact failures; retry transient; flag others for human input) before implementation so each phase is validated and committed independently.

summary: Error-Handling (1/4): Added utils/recovery.py — backup_directory/prepare_clean_dir/restore_directory (move existing artifacts to a timestamped <parent>/_backups copy before a clean rebuild), classify_failure (stale_state | transient | needs_human, with transient taking precedence), and retry_with_backoff (bounded exponential retry of transient failures). 15 unit tests in utils/graph_loader/tests/test_recovery.py.
why: A single dependency-free, tested home for the copy-then-replace, failure-classification, and retry primitives the builder and pipeline runner will consume.

summary: Error-Handling (2/4): KGBuildRunner.build_attack and build_capec now call recovery.prepare_clean_dir on the canonical directory instead of ensure_dir, so any existing on-disk canonical artifacts are moved to data/graphs/<dataset>/_backups/canonical-<ts> and each build writes into a clean directory. 2 new tests in utils/kg_builder/tests/test_build_recovery.py; full kg_builder suite green (62 passed).
why: A re-build that merged into an un-cleaned directory could leave a stale relationships.jsonl disagreeing with the freshly written allowlist schema, causing 'relationship type not in schema'. Clean rebuilds make this impossible while preserving the prior copy.

summary: Error-Handling (3/4): Made YoloRunner resilient. _step_build now validates existing canonical artifacts and, when stale/corrupt, rebuilds clean (the builder backs the old copy up) instead of blindly skipping; a clean rebuild that still fails is escalated as needs_input. Network/IO steps (docker start, load attack, load capec, verify) run through a _guarded retry-with-backoff that classifies failures: transient errors retry then fail, non-recoverable errors become a new needs_input status (symbol '?', halts abort-steps, non-zero exit in main.py). Summary table reports needs-input steps with a remediation hint. retry_with_backoff resolves time.sleep at call time so it is patchable. 15 new yolo tests; full util suite 139 passed.
why: Implements the requested policy: existing-artifact failures self-heal via backup-and-replace, transient errors retry, and genuinely stuck failures ask for human input instead of crashing opaquely.

summary: Error-Handling (4/4): Documented the recovery layer. Added utils/recovery.py and utils/yolo.py to the docs/structure.md utilities table with a 'Pipeline error handling' subsection (backup-and-replace under data/graphs/<dataset>/_backups, transient retry, NEEDS INPUT escalation), and added a 'One-command pipeline' subsection to README.md describing --yolo-all and its self-healing behavior.
why: Keep the repo map and operator docs truthful about the new module and the pipeline's error-handling guarantees.

summary: Authored docs/plans/specialist-agents-plan.md: a 6-phase plan for the two source-specific query specialists (Cypher/ATT&CK-Neo4j, Gremlin/CAPEC-Gremlin) built on one shared scaffold with four language-specific swap points (builder, validator, connector, normalizer), a shared evidence schema with provenance, federation into the planner workflow, a step-by-step notebook, and merge-to-main.

summary: Specialist Agents (1/6): Added the shared scaffold for the two query specialists under utils/specialists/ — input/output contracts (SpecialistTask, EvidenceRecord+Provenance, SpecialistResult, EvaluatorTrace), env-driven SpecialistConfig, the deterministic evidence emitter + contract check, the shared resolve-to-schema step (entity->card mapping, seed-id/T-number/CAPEC-id extraction, canonical join-endpoint, STIX-type pairing), the BaseValidator pre-run-gate orchestration, and the QuerySpecialist ReAct loop (intake->resolve->draft->gate->execute->assess->normalize->handoff) with capped redraft and full evaluator traces. 24 unit tests; planner suite still green (88).
why: Locks the shared/language-specific boundary and the evidence contract once, before either engine is built, so both specialists emit the schema synthesis joins on identically.

summary: Specialist Agents (2/6): Added the Cypher specialist (utils/specialists/cypher/) for MITRE ATT&CK on Neo4j — deterministic MATCH-template builder (technique->mitigations, group/tactic->techniques, node lookup, label scan), a static pre-run gate (single-statement, MATCH+RETURN, card label/edge membership, STIX-type/label pairing, write-clause rejection, LIMIT inject/clamp, and a new shared cap_reasons hook rejecting unbounded/over-depth variable-length paths), a READ_ACCESS Neo4j connector with per-query timeout, and a row->evidence normalizer. Registered the integration/live pytest marks. Live-verified T1047 -> M1038/M1040/M1018/M1026.
why: Brings the ATT&CK query specialist up green against the live Neo4j graph in isolation, proving the shared scaffold end-to-end before the harder Gremlin side.

summary: Specialist Agents (3/6): Added the Gremlin specialist (utils/specialists/gremlin/) for MITRE CAPEC — deterministic g.V() traversal builder (capec lookup, neighbors, the MAPS_TO ATT&CK join filtered to taxonomy ATTACK, label scan) emitting a single literal .limit bound, the heavier pre-run gate (g.V()/g.E() start, mutating-step rejection, hasLabel/out/in/both label+edge-direction checks against allowed_edge_patterns, and traversal-depth REJECTION via cap_reasons), a TinkerPop connector with per-query timeout, and an elementMap->evidence normalizer that derives CAPEC-N ids and emits T-prefixed ATTACK join values. Live-verified CAPEC-66 -> CWE-89/CWE-1286 and CAPEC-1 -> T1574.010. 89 specialist tests green.
why: Brings the CAPEC query specialist up green against the live Gremlin graph with the strict label/direction/depth validation property graphs require, completing both specialists in isolation.

summary: Specialist Agents (4/6): Wove the specialists into the planner workflow. Added utils/specialists/federation.py (SpecialistRouter/run_plan: dispatch each planner SubQuestion to the specialist serving its source, collect normalized evidence into a FederatedEvidence bundle with a join_index over the shared ATT&CK-technique-id key and cross-source-join detection — evidence, not prose), utils/specialists/cli.py (run_query_command: plan then run specialists, print queries/records/summaries/provenance JSON), and a main.py --query/--query-llm route mirroring --plan. Also made the seedless Cypher scan prefer substantive labels (Technique) over admin nodes (Matrix). Verified end-to-end live: credential-theft question routes to both sources, CAPEC MAPS_TO returns 177 ATTACK-mapped techniques, exit 0. 94 specialist tests green.
why: Individual specialists in isolation do not prove the pipeline; routing a real planner Plan through them with provenance intact is the federated query the project exists to demonstrate.

summary: Specialist Agents (5/6): Added notebooks/planning-schematic-agents.ipynb — a runnable step-by-step demo of the full planner -> specialists workflow (live probe, source-card schematic, plan, Cypher and Gremlin specialists with per-step evaluator traces, full federation, a real cross-source T-number join, and gate-rejection safety cases); executed headlessly end-to-end (exit 0). Hardened the Gremlin connector to confine its client + asyncio event loop to a dedicated worker thread so it runs inside a Jupyter kernel without the 'event loop already running' crash. Added docs/specialist_agents.md and updated README, docs/structure.md, and docs/goals.md (Wk 7-8 Cypher and Wk 8-9 Gremlin checked off).
why: Gives an inspectable, runnable demonstration of the federated query workflow against the live stack and documents the specialists' contract and four swap points.

summary: Workbench UI (2/8): Added web/lib/types.ts (TypeScript mirrors of the planner/specialist trace objects — Plan, SubQuestion, EvaluatorTrace, EvidenceRecord, Provenance, SpecialistResult, FederatedEvidence — plus UI view-model types and StageStatus/RunStatus enums), web/lib/fixtures.ts (the WMI->CAPEC sample run as a fully-typed WorkbenchRun with a real nested FederatedEvidence for the Raw JSON tab), and web/lib/conversations.ts. summary: Workbench UI (3/8): Built the full-height three-region AppShell (268px conversations rail / fluid center / 420px inspector, shadow-as-border seams, internal-scroll regions) and the HeaderBar (Ariadne thread-glyph wordmark, Analyst Workbench tag, live InfraStatusPill badges, Run Pipeline ghost button, Neo4j login). summary: Workbench UI (4/8): Built the left Conversations rail (grouped Today/Yesterday/This week list, active teal thread-edge, Plan/Query mode pills, New button) and the center chat thread: ThreadHeader, right-aligned UserMessage, the structured AnswerCard (MiniStepper status strip, grounded prose with inline ProvenanceChips, footer cross-source JoinChips, View-JSON/Copy/Export actions), and the Composer (Plan/Full-answer + deterministic/LLM toggles, Send). Added a WorkbenchProvider client context so provenance chips and stepper segments can focus inspector stages (consumed in phase 5).
why: These are the analyst's primary read/write surfaces; wiring the cross-panel focus context now lets the Answer Card drive the inspector once it is built.

summary: Workbench UI (5/8): Built the right Inspector — the product centerpiece. InspectorPanel (own collapsible aside with reopen rail), InspectorTabs (Trace/Evidence/Join/Raw), ProgressMeter, and the Trace timeline: a vertical thread with planner TraceStages (probe/draft/gate/emit, shield emphasis on the gate) and SpecialistLanes (backend badge, the eight micro-step checkpoints with shield+ring on the never-cut pre-run gate and normalize, the validated Cypher/Gremlin query via the highlighter, and expandable evidence records). Added Evidence/JoinIndex/RawJson tabs. Provenance chips and stepper segments now focus + scroll the right stage via the WorkbenchProvider; collapse reflows the chat to full width.
why: Seeing exactly what the agent did, step by step, is what turns a generic chat UI into a trustable analyst tool; the inspector renders the actual trace objects so the same components light up when a live stream replaces the fixture.

summary: Workbench UI (6/8): Made the UI animate on pipeline EVENTS. Added lib/runMachine.ts (useRunMachine: a timed event sequence flipping node statuses pending->running->pass, the shape a live SSE stream would emit) and lib/motion.ts (shared Motion variants incl. status-driven dot animation). Folded the machine into WorkbenchProvider (wrapped in MotionConfig reducedMotion=user) and wired status-reactive animation across the mini-stepper dots + outcome chip, the trace markers and the thread that grows as stages pass, the specialist micro-step cascade, the progress bar, the answer-card skeleton->reveal, tab cross-fades, and the collapse width. Added a RunController Replay button. Verified end-to-end: progress advances 0->2->4 stages, answer reveals on the answer event, no console errors.
why: The request is explicit that animations be an event-based approach so a future live workflow drives them; centralizing a status machine + Motion variants makes each part animate off a status prop, which is exactly the seam a real stream plugs into.

summary: Workbench UI (7/8): Made the workbench responsive and accessible. Below lg the inspector becomes a right slide-over drawer (shared InspectorContent extracted; InspectorPanel is now desktop-only, InspectorDrawer added with its own drawerOpen state defaulting closed + a floating reopen button); below md the conversations rail becomes a left slide-over via a header hamburger (MobileMenuButton + leftOpen). Decoupled desktop inline-collapse (inspectorOpen) from the mobile drawer (drawerOpen) with an openInspector() helper used by chips and the View-JSON action. Added aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-labels, kept teal focus rings, and honor prefers-reduced-motion via MotionConfig + CSS. The loading skeleton and answered/partial/no_sources states are type-driven.
why: Woven Dusk + ADA require intentionally-designed mobile (not just stacked) and color-plus-label status; the three-region shell needed drawer behavior so the dense inspector and rail work on small screens.

summary: Workbench UI (8/8): Updated docs for the Next.js webfront stack — global-project-rules layer table (React/Vite -> Next.js App Router + Tailwind v4 + Motion) and Commands (added 'cd web && npm test' Vitest line); docs/structure.md web tree label and the Web Demo section (new app/ + components/ + lib/ map, event-based run-state machine note, dev/build/lint/test commands). Added scoped negations (!web/lib/ and !web/lib/**) and committed the seven web/lib files. Merged main now passes npm run build, npm run lint, and npm test (7 passed).
why: web/lib is application source, not a Python build artifact; without un-ignoring it the merged webfront could not compile. Verified end-to-end on main after the fix.

summary: Added root app.py: a Python launcher for the Ariadne web server that verifies the Node toolchain, installs web/ JavaScript dependencies on first run (skippable with --skip-install, forceable with --install), and starts the Next.js app — dev with hot reload by default, or --prod for a production build+start, with --port/--host flags. Also pinned turbopack.root to web/ in web/next.config.ts so a stray lockfile elsewhere can't misdirect Turbopack root inference. Verified app.py boots the server to HTTP 200 with no lockfile warning.
why: The user asked for a single root entry point that runs everything the web server needs; app.py mirrors main.py's role for the Python side and removes the manual cd web && npm install && npm run dev steps.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (plan): staged plan for wiring the static Next.js workbench to the live Python backend — a new FastAPI service layer (api/) wrapping utils/ for live-source health, the federated query pipeline (real SSE stage events), LLM/connection config, and infra control; Next.js proxies /api and app.py launches both. Written to docs/plans/frontend-backend-integration.md.
why: The workbench is currently static (no fetch/API); the user wants it fully interactable — see Neo4j/Gremlin liveness, run conversational queries with a staged event sequence, and configure the LLM from the app, incorporating everything main.py can do.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (1/8): scaffolded the api/ FastAPI service and added GET /api/health. The health service probes each graph backend over TCP (per-backend live/down/starting verdict, never raising — unlike run_graph_health which raises ConnectionError) and folds in docker compose state so a booting container reads as 'starting'. Added fastapi, uvicorn[standard], httpx deps and the api package to the wheel targets. 5 pytest contract tests pass (shape, no-raise, docker-unavailable, uri parsing).
why: Every other endpoint depends on a running service and a stable JSON contract; live-source health is the simplest real capability and the first user-visible goal (is Neo4j/Gremlin up).

summary: Frontend↔Backend (2/8): added GET/PUT /api/config to view and edit the env-backed LLM and connection settings. GET resolves through PlannerConfig/SpecialistConfig.from_env() and redacts the Neo4j password (returns neo4j_password_set bool only); PUT validates (http base_url, positive timeout/max_tokens, bolt/ws URIs) and persists via utils.config.set_env_values which preserves .env layout and mirrors into os.environ so edits take effect on the next query without a restart. Documented the PLANNER_LLM_*/SPECIALIST_LLM_* keys in .env.example (section 8). 9 new pytest contract tests pass (14 total).
why: The user must configure the LLM (model, endpoint, enable flag, limits) directly within the app; this is the backend half of that settings form.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (3/8): added POST /api/query, a Server-Sent-Events stream of the federated pipeline. The sync generator reuses the planner→specialists→FederatedEvidence composition (mirroring run_query_command) and emits a real event at each boundary — status, probe (live sources with node counts), plan (with trace), per-specialist results as each completes, evidence bundle, and a server-composed grounded answer (from per-source summaries + the cross-source join index; the pipeline emits evidence, not prose). Starlette iterates the sync generator in its threadpool so blocking graph queries never stall the event loop. Exit codes mirror the CLI (2 no-cards, 1 partial, 0 clean). 8 stub-driven contract tests assert event order/shapes (22 total); validated end-to-end against the live stack (attack 2611 + capec 4888 nodes, 399 records, 84 cross-source correlations, exit 0).
why: This is the heart of the request: make the chat show the real sequence of events when a question is asked, driven by the actual federated query against Neo4j and Gremlin.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (4/8): added the web data layer. web/lib/api.ts is a typed client (getHealth/getConfig/putConfig + a streamQuery SSE helper that POSTs and parses event/data frames off the ReadableStream, since EventSource can't POST). web/lib/adapt.ts is the single backend→WorkbenchRun adapter: pure builders map the Plan/FederatedEvidence/probe/answer payloads onto live sources, four planner stages, per-source lanes with the eight micro-steps, evidence rows, join candidates, and the answer (chips + cross-source join pairs) — components stay unchanged. Added API/SSE wire types to types.ts and a Next rewrite proxying /api/* to FastAPI (same-origin, no CORS). 9 Vitest adapter cases reproduce the canonical WMI run from the federated bundle (16 web tests total); npm build, lint, test all green.
why: The front end must consume real backend data without changing every component; a typed client plus one adapter is the clean seam, and the proxy keeps the browser same-origin.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (5/8): rewired the run lifecycle to live events. runMachine.ts now holds the active WorkbenchRun and a submit() that opens the /api/query SSE stream, advancing liveStatus and rebuilding the run via the adapter as each event arrives (probe→plan→per-specialist→evidence→answer→done); the offline timed replay() is kept for the Run/Replay demo controls. A new client Workbench component bridges the context run to the three regions as props (every presentational component unchanged). The Composer is now interactive (controlled textarea, mode/drafter toggles, Enter-to-send, disabled while running) and AnswerCard handles the error state. Validated live in-browser: submitting a question streams to a real answer (399 records, 84 cross-source correlations) with lanes built from live Cypher/Gremlin data, the Running… state shows, and there are no console errors; build/lint/test green.
why: This delivers the conversational flow and the staged, animated reveal driven by the real federated query — the core 'sequence of events when we ask a question'.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (6/8): live infra status + in-app settings. A new InfraStatusBar client component polls GET /api/health every 5s so the header pills reflect real Neo4j/Gremlin reachability (HeaderBar is now a client component); the pill renders 'LIVE' without a count when the TCP probe has no node count. A new SettingsPanel modal (opened from the header gear) loads GET /api/config and edits the planner+specialist LLM knobs (enable, base URL, model, timeout, max tokens) and the graph connection (URIs, user, write-only password) via PUT /api/config, with validation errors surfaced and a 'Saved · applies to the next query' confirmation. Added a GearIcon and settingsOpen state to the workbench context. Validated live: pills present, panel loads all sections (12 inputs), and a planner-model edit round-trips and persists through the proxy. build/lint/test green.
why: Closes the two remaining priority goals — a live is-it-up indicator and an in-app form for the env-backed LLM/connection settings.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (7/8): infra control actions covering the remaining main.py modes. POST /api/admin streams an SSE log feed for docker start/stop/status, graph health/load/verify, and data download/build — each runs in a worker thread while a temporary root-logging handler forwards the modules' real log output as 'log' events, then a 'done' event with ok/message (failures reported, not raised). A new settings 'Infrastructure & data' section (InfraActions) runs these with a dataset/graph selector and a streamed log console; api.ts gained a generic postSseStream reader shared by streamQuery and a new streamAdmin. 8 stub-driven backend tests assert event order/validation/handler cleanup (30 backend total). Validated live end-to-end through the proxy and UI (graph-health streams real logs → ✓ completed).
why: The user asked to incorporate every main.py capability; these host/admin operations complete that surface, exposed as a streamed admin console.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (8/8): made app.py launch both processes and refreshed the docs. app.py now starts the FastAPI service (via `uv run uvicorn`, falling back to the interpreter) and the Next.js app together, passing API_PORT so the web proxy targets the service, with coordinated Ctrl+C shutdown and --api-port/--prod flags. docs/structure.md gained an api/ section + a rewritten web section and updated 'not yet in repo' (synthesis prose agent only); global-project-rules added the api/ layer, the app.py launcher, and the `pytest api/tests/` + `python app.py` commands. Full regression green: 30 api tests, 16 web tests, npm lint + build, and a clean app.py dual-launch boot (proxied health + full query SSE → answered, exit 0).
why: app.py must run everything the web server needs; with a required backend it has to start both, and the canonical docs must describe the two-process architecture so future agents don't assume the static-only UI.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (plan): wrote docs/plans/full-pipeline-visibility.md. Audit found the backend already streams the complete pipeline (plan.to_dict with iteration trace, per-specialist result.to_dict with raw query + full records + 6-step evaluator traces, full FederatedEvidence with join index) but the front end discards most of it and the chat is single-run. The 6-phase plan exposes a multi-turn chat, full trace depth (planner iterations + evaluator reasons/detail + task metadata + skipped/unsupported), uncapped evidence with full properties/provenance, a multi-payload raw-JSON surface incl. the literal SSE event stream, and adds the last missing main.py admin modes (graph-stop, yolo-all).
why: User asked the workbench to do everything main.py can — full chat, full trace, evidence and raw JSON, end to end. The gap is front-end exposure + multi-turn chat, not the backend.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (1/6): multi-turn chat + raw event/payload capture. Replaced the single-run model with a conversation of turns in runMachine.ts (runs[] + activeRunId + streamingRunId + selectRun/newConversation); each turn now also retains the literal ordered SSE event log and the raw probe/plan/answer payloads (new WorkbenchRun fields, threaded through buildRun). ChatThread renders the full thread (clicking a turn selects it; empty state when cleared); the left rail is driven by real turns with a New action; AnswerCard/MiniStepper take a `live` prop so only the streaming turn animates while past turns render their own baked status. Validated live: asked two questions, all turns persisted with independent ANSWERED/PARTIAL chips, rail switching moved the inspector turn label, and New reset to empty. build + lint + 18 web tests green.
why: The user asked for full chat interfaces; the workbench was single-run with a static mock rail. Multi-turn state + per-turn raw capture is the foundation the deeper trace/evidence/raw-JSON views build on.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (2/6): full trace depth in the inspector. Re-grounded the specialist lane micro-steps to the SIX real EvaluatorTrace steps (intake, resolve, pre-run gate, execute, assess, normalize) — the invented draft/handoff steps are gone. Each lane now renders a Task block (entities, seed_ids, join_key, limits, rationale), an Evaluator trace section (one expandable LaneTraceRow per trace entry, including gate/execute retries, revealing reasons + the full detail JSON), and an error line when a specialist fails. The planner stages now expose the full plan.trace iteration history (gate stage) plus full sub-question detail (draft) and joins/unsupported-with-reasons/assumptions/rationale (emit). TraceTab gained a Skipped & unsupported section that renders when present. Validated live: a query showed all six pills, iteration trace with drafter, expandable detail JSON (timing_ms/template/injected), and task metadata. build + lint + 20 web tests green, no console errors.
why: User asked to see the full trace; the UI was discarding the planner loop history, per-step reasons/detail, task metadata, and skipped/unsupported, and showing two micro-steps the pipeline never emits.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (3/6): uncapped, fully-detailed evidence. The adapter no longer truncates (dropped the 200-row evidence cap and the 6-per-lane cap) and now carries each record's complete properties/related/join_values plus full provenance (the exact query, record_id, timestamp) into the view-model. The Evidence tab gained a text filter (by id/name/label) with a 'showing X of Y' counter and incremental reveal (60 + Show more / Show all) so hundreds of records stay responsive without silent loss; each row expands to the full record JSON and the provenance query (cypher/gremlin). Specialist lanes gained the same reveal (initial 8). Added 3 adapter tests incl. a 250-record no-cap assertion. Validated live against a ~399-record query: lanes showed '177/222 total · showing 8', the Evidence tab filtered (2 of 4) and expanded a record to full JSON + Cypher provenance.
why: User asked to see the full evidence; the UI was capping at 200/6 records and collapsing each to a one-line blob, hiding properties, adjacency, and the provenance query.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (4/6): multi-payload raw-JSON surface + literal SSE event stream, and a tab-switch fix. RawJsonTab now takes the whole run and offers a payload selector — Events / Plan / Probe / Evidence / Answer — each a copyable pretty-printed JSON block; Events renders the turn's ordered SSE log (one color-coded entry per event with its data) so the pipeline is visible start to finish. While validating, found and fixed a real defect: InspectorContent used AnimatePresence mode='wait', and the heavier Phase-2 trace tab's nested-motion subtree never completed its exit, which stalled ALL inspector tab switching; replaced it with a remount+fade of the active tab (no exit wait). Validated live: switched across all four tabs, Events showed '11 events · pipeline order', Plan payload showed request/sub_questions/trace/iteration, copy buttons present.
why: User asked for raw JSON and to see the full evidence-backed pipeline start to finish; only the federated bundle was exposed and the event log/plan/probe/answer were not. The tab-switch stall (regression from the richer trace tab) had to be fixed for any of this to be reachable.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (5/6): admin completeness — graph-stop and yolo-all. The two remaining main.py modes are now reachable from the app: api/models.py adds 'graph-stop' and 'yolo-all' to the AdminAction literal; api/services/infra.py dispatches graph-stop → docker_stop_service(target) (reusing the request's graph field) and yolo-all → YoloRunner().run() (summarizing steps/failed/needs_input), both streamed through the existing log-forwarding SSE wrapper. Validated live: both buttons render in settings and the admin SSE path streams '✓ graph-health completed' end to end (destructive graph-stop/yolo-all intentionally not executed against the live stack).
why: User asked to incorporate every main.py capability; graph-stop and yolo-all were the only CLI modes not yet exposed in the app.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (6/6): docs + full regression + merge. docs/structure.md now describes the multi-turn chat, the full Trace/Evidence/Raw-JSON+event-stream inspector surfaces, and the completed admin coverage (graph-stop, yolo-all) on POST /api/admin. Full regression green in the worktree: 35 api tests, 23 web tests, npm lint + build, and a clean app.py dual-launch (proxied query → answered, exit 0). Merged the full-pipeline-visibility worktree into main (commit only, not pushed per the session override).
why: The workbench now does everything main.py can — full chat, full trace, full evidence, raw JSON end to end — so the canonical docs must reflect it and the feature is merged.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (1/5): independent raw recount oracle. New utils/graph_loader/fixture_qa package with raw_counts.py that recounts ATT&CK node labels straight from the raw STIX bundle and CAPEC AttackPattern/Category/View from the raw XML, deliberately NOT reusing the build preprocessors so a systematic build drop is catchable. Tracks excluded revoked/deprecated (ATT&CK) and retired-status patterns (CAPEC). 5 unit tests over synthetic fixtures, all green; validated against real data (ATT&CK 2611 nodes, 157 revoked + 251 deprecated; CAPEC 615/78/13).
why: Existing --graph verify only compares live DB against the build manifest; there was no independent raw->manifest reconciliation, which is the highest-value fixture-QA check per the BRON/GraphKer findings.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (2/5): live referential-integrity store methods. Added ReferentialIntegrityResult to models and a referential_integrity() method to the GraphStore contract, implemented for Neo4j (Cypher dangling/id-less queries), Gremlin (traversal for id-less vertices and edges with id-less endpoints), and the in-memory test store. 3 new tests plus the store-contract suite green; validated live: both running graphs report 0 dangling edges and 0 id-less nodes.

summary: Component Evaluation (1/8): shared statistics scaffold. New utils/evaluation/ package with stats.py — pure-Python percentile (type-7 linear interpolation, matching numpy's default; mean deliberately omitted since latency is right-skewed), Wilson binomial score interval (stays in [0,1] and behaves at the x==n ceiling where the deterministic query builder lives), and a seeded percentile-bootstrap CI (byte-reproducible). 14 hermetic tests in utils/evaluation/tests/test_stats.py assert known-input percentiles (1..100 -> p50=50.5/p95=95.05/p99=99.01), Wilson symmetry/ceiling/point-containment, and bootstrap determinism.
why: Every downstream component metric (VA/EX pass rates, latency percentiles) needs the same CI/percentile math; building it once as a pure hermetic module keeps every scorer consistent and testable before any live data is involved.

summary: Component Evaluation (2/8): planner sub-question-quality sub-score + dev/holdout reporting + drafter selector. scorer.py now measures decomposition beyond entity recall — count_correct (right number of sub-questions, defaulting to one per expected source), routing_correct (each sub-question routed to an expected source and every expected source covered), and dependency_correct (join declared iff the question is multi-hop) — combined into decomposition_score and a composite sub_question_quality; aggregate() adds mean_sub_question_quality/decomposition and routing/count/dependency accuracy rates. corpus.py gains an optional expected_sub_question_count override. run_eval.py adds a --drafter deterministic|llm|hybrid selector (LLM best-effort via the config factory, falls back to deterministic and reports which ran) and a dev-vs-holdout breakdown. 7 new tests; planner suite 97/97; corpus still 7/7 pass_rate 1.0.
why: 'Sub-question quality' needs the decomposition check (count/routing/dependency) the proposal names, not just entity recall; adding it before corpus expansion means the new cases are scored on the complete metric set, and scoring both drafters is the honest deterministic-floor + LLM-lift presentation.

summary: Component Evaluation (3/8): planner corpus expanded 7 -> 31 (24 generated + 7 curated), snapshot-derived. New build_corpus.py derives single-source expected plans from the specialist golden banks: a candidate is kept only when the deterministic planner selects the gold source (source-recall==1.0) and the plan is schema-adherent, capped at 3 per builder-template, with every excluded question reported (9 unroutable bare lookups, 8 adversarial, 12 template-cap) — no silent drops. Cases carry origin (curated|generated) and tier; a deterministic quarter is frozen into holdout. Corpus-wide hard guarantees hold (source_recall/schema/honesty == 1.0); the honest measurement picture surfaces real findings — precision 0.887 (7 unnecessary source calls from mitigation/mapping over-routing), pass_rate 0.774. Regression tests split: strict pass on the 7 curated anchors, hard-guarantee + reproducibility checks on the generated set (skip when data cards unbuilt). Planner suite 99/99.
why: A 7-case corpus is too small to be statistically defensible for source-selection scoring; deriving from the specialist banks makes the planner and specialists answer the same catalogue and turns the planner's real routing imprecision into reported, diagnosable metrics.

summary: Component Evaluation (4/8): hermetic Query Validity (VA) scorer. New utils/specialists/evalset/score_validity.py drives each specialist's own builder+validator through the same resolve->draft->gate retry loop as base.py but stops before any DB call, so VA (the grammar / valid-accuracy metric) is fully hermetic and reproducible. Reports first-pass VA and post-retry VA per specialist per tier with Wilson CIs; schema-boundary questions (no query drafted) are reported separately, never in the denominator. Result confirms the design: attack 30/30 and capec 21/21 first-pass VA (100%, 2 Asset boundaries excluded) — the deterministic builder never free-generates, so VA sits at the ceiling and any later EX miss points at routing/seeds, not malformed queries. 5 hermetic tests.
why: VA is the community-standard syntactic-validity metric; because the gate runs before the database, VA is measurable without live infra, and near-ceiling VA is the evidence that Ariadne sidesteps the generation-hallucination failure mode of free-form text-to-query systems.

summary: Component Evaluation (5/8): snapshot-derived EX gold + Execution Accuracy scorer + error taxonomy. questions.py now attaches an ex_gold block (full expected id set + the id surface to compare: node=the looked-up node, neighbors=id_pool minus the seed inputs, join=T-prefixed ATTACK join values only) derived from the gold bank; technique-fanout gold is the top-level Technique slice (matching the builder's sub-technique roll-up) so a correct answer is not penalised. New score_execution.py runs each bank question live and reports exact-set-match EX and precision/recall/F1 with Wilson CIs, bucketing every miss (missing_hop/over_broad/mismatch/empty_when_nonempty/fabricated_nonempty/boundary_failure/cardinality). Live result: attack 32/32 and capec 21/21 exact-match, precision 1.0, empty taxonomy — the deterministic specialists reproduce the independently-parsed snapshot, which also confirms ingestion faithfulness. score_validity.build_specialists now loads .env so the live path connects. 9 tests (hermetic taxonomy/pool + live EX); evalset+golden 140/140.
why: EX (result-set correctness, phrasing-invariant) is the community-standard text-to-query metric; partial credit + a taxonomy turn the pass/fail banks into diagnosable findings, and comparing the live graph to independently-derived gold doubles as an ingest-faithfulness check.

summary: Component Evaluation (6/8): bounded-execution safety-adherence audit + adversarial gate probes. New score_safety.py independently audits every gate-accepted query for read-only + LIMIT-present-and-<=cap + no unbounded/over-depth traversal (adherence 30/30 attack, 21/21 capec, zero breaches), and fires hand-crafted adversarial drafts (writes, DETACH DELETE, CALL{}, LOAD CSV, unbounded/over-depth var-length paths, addV/addE/drop/property, unknown labels) straight at the validator asserting a 100% block rate. The unknown-label probe surfaced a real gate gap: the Gremlin validator's hasLabel/out/in/both regexes matched only double-quoted labels, so a single-quoted unknown label (g.V().hasLabel('Secret')) bypassed schema conformance; hardened the four regexes to accept both quote styles. Now 10/10 and 7/7 probes blocked, no leaks. New fixtures/adversarial_probes.py; 6 hermetic tests; full specialist suite 290/290.
why: Safety-constraint adherence is named in the proposal but never scored; the gate is the enforcement point, so auditing accepted queries and probing it with malicious drafts is the honest hermetic test — and the probe did its job, finding and fixing a single-quote schema-validation bypass before it could matter.

summary: Component Evaluation (7/8): per-stage timing hooks + segmented latency harness. base.py now additively records timing_ms on the gate/assess/normalize trace steps (execute already had it) — no behavioural change.
